plumbing.review:
**[P2] Shortening loses the original paragraph break before instructions.** [comments.go:50](comments.go:50) trims trailing body whitespace, but callers such as [plancomments.go:40](plancomments.go:40) supply only one leading newline in `closing`; the other remains in the body. Even when removing collapsed details makes a proposal fit, `…I merge it.\n\nTo ratify…` becomes `…I merge it.\nTo ratify…`. Other affected callers can attach instructions to a preceding list or blockquote. This violates the plan’s requirement to preserve separating whitespace. Move the complete separator into `closing`, preserving byte-for-byte short output.

The acceptance tests miss this boundary: their exact-output details-removal case explicitly supplies both newlines ([closing_commands_accept_test.go:235](closing_commands_accept_test.go:235)), while real callers’ instructions receive substring checks.

Otherwise, the change stays within the authorized files, migrates the instruction-bearing callers, and matches surrounding Go style. The acceptance source matches the ratified plan; I found no test-specific behavior, weakened checks, added host/network access, or secret exposure. [tests.txt:1](tests.txt:1) reports all checks passed; I did not rerun builds during this read-only review. No documentation contradiction surfaced. Recording the decision remains the merger’s responsibility under [plan.json:3](plan.json:3).

VERDICT: changes needed — Preserve complete closing separators and verify real callers retain their paragraph breaks after shortening.

usage.summary:
